units.statement: A trans-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis of 688,808 major depression cases and 4,364,225 controls from 29 countries identified 697 independent associations at 635 loci, of which 293 (46%) were novel, substantially expanding the depression association map beyond previous European-only analyses.
source_quotes: About half (293/635; 46%) of the discovered loci were novel MD associations

In a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of 688,808 individuals with major depression (MD) and 4,364,225 controls from 29 countries across diverse and admixed ancestries, we identify 697 associations at 635 loci, 293 of which are novel.
The European-only analysis identified 622 SNPs in 570 regions with a net change in the full meta-analysis of 65 (142 regions gained, 77 regions became non-significant).

units.statement: Including ancestrally diverse and admixed cohorts in the GWAS meta-analysis yielded 100 additional loci beyond the European-only analysis, increasing the effective sample size through ancestry-aware modeling and demonstrating that trans-ancestry sampling expands locus discovery and enables genetic risk prediction across ancestry groups.

units.statement: Integrative fine-mapping, SNP-based prioritization (PolyFun/SuSiE), transcriptome-wide association (TWAS), and proteome-wide association (PWAS) analyses identified 308 high-confidence depression-associated gene or protein associations, with convergence across methods for 15 genes including CYP7B1, DCC, FURIN, and DRD2, implicating multiple biological pathways rather than a single molecular mechanism.

units.statement: Depression-associated genetic variation is enriched in neuronal cell types including excitatory and inhibitory neurons, multiple inhibitory neuron subcategories, medium spiny neurons, and peptidergic neurons across midbrain, amygdala, hippocampus, thalamus, and cortex, with the strongest new signals in amygdala excitatory neurons and MGE/CGE interneurons in both mouse and human single-cell analyses.

Our results confirm and extend previous findings showing the enrichment of expression signals in excitatory and inhibitory neurons.

Our results confirm and extend previous findings showing the enrichment of expression signals in excitatory and inhibitory neurons. Importantly, the increased power in this genetic analysis provided additional evidence for involvement of amygdala and hippocampal excitatory neurons, including granule cells and medium spiny neurons.

units.statement: Depression genetic association signals are significantly enriched for gene targets of antidepressants (ATC class N06A) and other drug classes including antipsychotics (N05A), identifying possible repurposing opportunities for compounds such as pregabalin, modafinil, and several anti-cancer therapies, though the enrichment test is non-directional and cannot distinguish therapeutic from risk-exacerbating mechanisms.

units.statement: Polygenic scores trained on European or multi-ancestry GWAS summary statistics predict major depression case-control status across ancestries, explaining up to 5.8% of liability-scale variance in European cohorts (a substantial increase from 3.2% in prior studies), with prediction significantly lower in African-ancestry studies and no consistent improvement from multi-ancestry over European-only training sets.

units.statement: SNP-based heritability of major depression in European ancestries is estimated at 8.4% (SE 0.07%) on the liability scale, with the study estimating polygenicity at approximately 6% and a selection parameter near 0.54, implying that common SNP effects explain roughly 69% of the additive genetic variance for major depression, consistent with a highly polygenic architecture and highlighting the need for larger and more globally representative samples.
